Source [S2] confirms this definition: $G^? = T_{x,y,z}(G)$ where $T_{x,y,z} = arg max_{T_{x,y,z}} B(T_{x,y,z}(G))$. Source [S3] also defines the canonical representation as $g^* = arg max_{S_{x,y,z}} B(S_{x,y,z}(g))$. All sources consistently support the claim.
